key: A joint family in Kerala has a grandfather
name: ch26_grandfather_household_chairman
alt: An elderly grandfather sits proudly at the head of a family dinner table as the household chairman while his daughter-in-law quietly pays the electricity bill on her phone behind him.
scene: A warm evening scene inside a Kerala joint-family home, seen from the side at table height. Centre-left: a long low dining table with steel plates, a banana leaf with rice and a bowl of sambar. At its head sits the grandfather, late seventies, white mundu and cream half-sleeve shirt, thick spectacles, grey moustache, sitting noticeably upright with his chest out and a small satisfied smile, one hand raised in a gentle blessing gesture. Beside him a son in his forties, blue shirt, leans in respectfully holding a printed brochure for a new refrigerator, asking for approval; a small green tick bubble floats above the grandfather's raised hand to show his blessing is the step that counts. Right side, a little behind, in a doorway to the kitchen: the daughter-in-law, mid thirties, plum sari, hair in a bun, stands half-turned away and quietly taps her phone, paying the electricity bill; an inset bubble from her phone shows a small bill card with a green tick and the word "PAID". On the wall behind the table hang a framed family photo and a brass oil lamp. A faint upward arrow beside the grandfather's shoulders suggests him sitting a little taller. Lighting is soft and golden, the mood affectionate and calm, nobody is embarrassed. Labels: "CHAIRMAN" in large letters above the grandfather's head near the top-left of the image.

key: A schoolteacher in Chennai catches a boy copying homework
name: ch26_teacher_copied_homework
alt: Split picture: on the left a teacher holds a boy's copied notebook up in front of a staring class; on the right she talks to him quietly at her desk after the bell.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same Chennai classroom with a green chalkboard in both halves and the same two characters. The teacher is in her forties, mustard cotton sari, hair in a plait with jasmine, spectacles; the boy is about twelve, white school shirt, navy shorts, school tie. LEFT panel: the teacher stands at the front holding the boy's open notebook high above her head, mouth open mid-sentence, while the boy stands beside his desk with head bowed and shoulders hunched, cheeks flushed; three classmates at their desks turn to stare, one pointing and one giggling behind a hand, and a small red exclamation badge floats near the boy. A dark rain cloud drifts above the boy's head to show lasting dread. RIGHT panel: the bell has rung, the room is empty, a wall clock reads just after one; the teacher sits at her desk with the notebook lying closed, leaning forward kindly with one open palm, and the boy stands beside her listening, upright, embarrassed but calm, holding a fresh notebook and a pencil to redo the work. A small green tick floats above the fresh notebook. Lighting is bright school daylight from tall windows. Labels: "IN FRONT" at the top of the left panel, "IN PRIVATE" at the top of the right panel.

key: A wedding caterer in Jaipur hires extra cooks
name: ch26_caterer_season_goodbye
alt: Split picture: one caterer ignores a seasonal helper at season's end; another shares chai with him and invites him back in October, and next year that caterer's phone rings first.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves set at the back of a Jaipur catering kitchen at the end of the wedding season, with big copper degchis stacked and a calendar on the wall. LEFT panel: a catering owner, fifties, white kurta and red Rajasthani turban, sits turned away scrolling his phone, ignoring a young helper, early twenties, saffron apron, who walks off toward the gate with a cloth bag over his shoulder, head down; a crossed-out phone icon hangs between them to show no call will come. RIGHT panel: a second owner, fifties, cream kurta and spectacles, sits on a low stool facing another young helper in a saffron apron; both hold small glass cups of chai and smile. Beside them sits a plate of bright orange jalebis. A speech bubble from the owner holds a small wall-calendar page reading "OCT" with a green tick. In the lower-right corner, a small inset circle shows the following October: the helper's phone ringing with little vibration marks, the second owner's face on its screen. Mood: left cool and empty, right warm, late-afternoon golden light. Labels: "SILENCE" at the top of the left panel, "COME BACK" at the top of the right panel.

key: A cricket coach at a district academy
name: ch26_keeper_joins_rival
alt: A coach shouts at a teenage wicketkeeper in front of the whole squad, and an arrow leads to the same boy later keeping brilliantly for a rival club.
scene: A wide outdoor scene at a district cricket academy ground, dusty outfield, practice nets in the background, evening sun. Left-centre: the coach, forties, tracksuit with a whistle around his neck and a cap, leans forward shouting, one finger jabbing, a jagged red speech bubble with an exclamation mark coming from his mouth. In front of him stands a teenage wicketkeeper, about sixteen, white kit, big keeping gloves and pads, eyes down, mumbling, with a small grey bubble holding a sun and a curving ball symbol to show his excuse about the light and the swing. Behind them, three squad-mates in white stand in a line watching with arms folded, one smirking; three dropped red balls lie on the grass near the keeper's feet. A long dashed arrow curves from the keeper toward the right side of the image, into a large round inset: the same boy now in a different coloured kit, teal shirt with a coral cap, diving sideways to take a clean catch behind the stumps, a big grin, a green tick above his gloves. The academy side looks dull and tense; the inset looks bright and alive. Labels: "RIVAL CLUB" just above the round inset on the right.

key: At a big family function, a new daughter-in-law
name: ch26_biryani_mother_in_law_shield
alt: At a crowded family function, a mother-in-law steps in front of a critical aunt to defend her nervous daughter-in-law's too-salty first biryani and promises a second try next Sunday.
scene: A busy family function in a home courtyard, strings of marigolds overhead, guests in the background eating from plates. Centre: a huge biryani handi on a stand, lid off, steam rising, a ladle resting in it, and a small salt shaker with a few white grains spilling to show the excess salt. Left: an aunt, sixties, green silk sari, hand raised with a pointing finger and mouth open as she starts to comment, a small grey speech bubble with a salt shaker symbol beginning above her. Between the aunt and the young woman, the mother-in-law, late fifties, maroon sari, steps forward with one arm stretched out like a shield, smiling broadly and speaking loudly to the room, her other hand resting on the daughter-in-law's shoulder. Right: the new daughter-in-law, mid twenties, coral salwar suit, dupatta, holding a serving spoon, eyes glistening with a single tear but lifting her head. A large white speech bubble from the mother-in-law contains a small calendar page reading "SUN" beside a small biryani handi with a green tick, showing the promise of next Sunday's second try. Warm afternoon light, the tension draining out of the moment. Labels: "SAVED FACE" in large letters across the top centre of the image.

key: A traffic policeman in Mumbai stops a scooter rider
name: ch26_traffic_two_constables
alt: Split picture: one constable lectures a scooter rider loudly at a crowded junction while people stare; another speaks quietly at the roadside; both riders get the same challan.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves set at a busy Mumbai road junction with a traffic signal showing red. LEFT panel: in the middle of the junction a traffic constable, khaki uniform, white cap, whistle, leans toward a scooter rider, office shirt and helmet, and shouts with a wagging finger, a big jagged speech bubble with an exclamation mark coming from him. Three onlookers stand at the edge, a woman with a shopping bag, a man at a bus stop and a boy, all staring and one pointing. The rider looks away, jaw tight, with a small dark scribble cloud above his helmet to show him muttering for days. RIGHT panel: at the quiet roadside under a tree, a second constable, same uniform, stands calmly beside a parked scooter, writing on a small notepad, one open palm toward the signal; the rider stands with his helmet under his arm, nodding, calm. Nobody stares. At the bottom of each panel, the same small paper challan slip with the word "FINE" and an identical green tick sits in the corner, showing both riders pay the same. Lighting: humid Mumbai daylight, the left side noisy, the right side settled. Labels: "LOUD" at the top of the left panel, "QUIET" at the top of the right panel.
